recipes.name: Neapolitan Pizza
recipes.description: A classic, thin-crust pizza topped with fresh, simple ingredients, exhibiting the perfect balance of chewy crust and bright tomato acidity.
instructions: Dissolve yeast and salt in warm water. Gradually add flour and knead for 15 mins until smooth.
Divide dough into 3 balls; let rise at room temperature for 8 hours.
Stretch dough by hand into thin circles, leaving a thicker rim (cornicione).
Spread crushed tomatoes over dough, top with mozzarella and fresh basil, and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake in a preheated pizza oven at 900°F (480°C) for 90 seconds, or in a home oven at maximum temperature on a pizza stone for 7-10 minutes.
recipes.funFact: Authentic Neapolitan Pizza is protected by the European Union as a Traditional Speciality Guaranteed (TSG) dish and its art is UNESCO intangible heritage.

recipes.name: Pad Thai
recipes.description: A vibrant, sweet-savory stir-fried rice noodle dish featuring balanced notes of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar, ubiquitous in Thai street food culture.
instructions: Soak rice noodles in lukewarm water for 30-45 minutes until pliable but firm.
Whisk tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar over low heat to form the sauce base.
Heat oil in a wok, stir-fry shrimp or tofu until lightly browned.
Push protein aside, crack egg into wok, and scramble.
Add drained noodles and tamarind sauce. Stir-fry rapidly until noodles absorb liquid.
Toss in bean sprouts and garlic chives for 1 minute. Serve hot, garnished with crushed peanuts and lime.
recipes.funFact: Pad Thai was actively promoted by the Thai government in the 1930s to foster national identity and reduce rice consumption during economic hardships.

recipes.name: Tacos al Pastor
recipes.description: Thinly sliced, marinated pork cooked on a vertical spit, heavily influenced by Lebanese shawarma tradition but local-focused with authentic Mexican spices.
ingredients: Finely chopped cilantro and white onion
instructions: Blend guajillo chiles, achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, and oregano into a smooth marinade.
Coat pork slices in the marinade; cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (ideally overnight).
Layer meat slices closely tightly together to roast. In a home kitchen, sear in a smoking-hot skillet or layer on skewers and roast at 400°F (200°C) until charred.
Thinly slice the cooked meat.
Warm corn tortillas, pile on sliced pork, and top with chopped onion, cilantro, and a small wedge of roasted pineapple.
recipes.funFact: The phrase 'Al Pastor' translates literally to 'in the style of the shepherd', nodding to the Lebanese immigrant origins of the cooking method.

recipes.name: Boeuf Bourguignon
recipes.description: An exemplary, slow-braised French beef stew cooked elegantly in rich red Burgundy wine, beef stock, and aromatic root vegetables.
instructions: Crisp bacon lardons in a large Dutch oven; remove and reserve. Brown beef cubes in the rendered bacon fat, then remove.
Sauté chopped onions and carrots in the remaining fat until soft.
Return beef to pot, sprinkle with flour, and toss to coat for 2 minutes.
Pour in wine and beef stock. Add bouquet garni and cooked bacon. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in a preheated oven at 325°F (160°C) for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Sauté pearl onions and mushrooms separately; fold into stew 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.funFact: What started as a rustic peasant dish to tenderize tough cuts of meat was elevated to haute cuisine by legendary chef Auguste Escoffier in the early 20th century.

recipes.name: Feijoada
recipes.description: A deeply flavorful, heavy stew of black beans, pork, and beef, considered the absolute pinnacle of Brazilian comfort food.
instructions: Soak dry black beans and salted meats separately in water overnight. Drain before cooking.
In a very large heavy pot, combine beans, meats, bay leaves, and the whole orange. Cover completely with water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer gently for approximately 2 to 2.5 hours until beans are tender.
In a skillet, fry bacon, then cook chopped onions and garlic until translucent.
Ladle a cup of beans from the main pot into the skillet, mash them to create a paste, and pour back into the stew to thicken it.
Simmer uncovered for another 20 minutes. Discard orange and serve with rice.
recipes.funFact: Feijoada is widely celebrated as Brazil's national dish, traditionally eaten at leisure during Saturday afternoons with family.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Biryani
recipes.description: A regal, highly aromatic rice dish made with long-grain basmati rice and marinated meat, slow-cooked together using the classic sealed 'dum' technique.
ingredients: 4 Large Onions (sliced and deep-fried until golden)
1 tsp Saffron Threads (soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk)
Whole Spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves)
instructions: Marinate meat with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, half the fried onions, mint, cilantro, and biryani spices for 2+ hours.
Parboil basmati rice with whole spices until it is only 70% cooked; drain thoroughly.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, layer the marinated raw meat at the bottom.
Layer the parboiled rice over the meat. Top with remaining fried onions, chopped herbs, melted ghee, and saffron milk.
Seal the pot tightly with dough or foil, cover with a heavy lid, and cook on low heat (Dum) for 45 minutes allowing the steam to cook everything perfectly.
recipes.funFact: The historic Nizams of Hyderabad boasted legendary royal kitchens where chefs created nearly 50 distinctive variations using unique meats like quail and deer.

recipes.name: New England Clam Chowder
recipes.description: A thick, velvety, and rich seafood soup featuring tender clams, salty pork, and hearty potatoes in a smooth cream base.
instructions: Render diced bacon/salt pork in a heavy pot until beautifully crisp; remove bacon and set aside.
Add butter to the fat, then sauté the diced onions until translucent.
Sprinkle in flour, stirring constantly for 2 minutes to create a smooth roux base.
Slowly whisk in the reserved clam juice and seafood stock to avoid lumps. Add cubed potatoes and thyme.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes until potatoes are completely tender.
Reduce heat to low, stir in chopped clams and heavy cream. Warm through for 5 minutes without boiling. Garnish with bacon.
recipes.funFact: Traditional New England chowder strictly forbids tomatoes. In 1939, a statutory bill was introduced in Maine to make adding tomatoes to clam chowder illegal.

recipes.name: Edomae Sushi
recipes.description: The quintessential style of modern sushi, featuring precisely seasoned vinegared rice topped with fresh, traditionally cured or treated seafood.
ingredients: 200g Sushi-Grade Raw Fish (Tuna, Salmon, or Sea Bass)
instructions: Rinse rice multiple times until water runs clear; cook in a rice cooker with slightly less water than normal.
Mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt over low heat until dissolved. Fold gently into cooked hot rice using a slicing motion; cool to body temp.
Slice fresh fish at a 45-degree angle into clean, uniform rectangles.
Wet hands with water-vinegar mix. Shape a small oblong ball of rice (approx. 20g) in your palm.
Dab a tiny speck of wasabi onto the fish slice, place fish over the rice ball, and press gently with two fingers to mold together perfectly.
recipes.funFact: Edomae means 'in front of Edo' (old Tokyo). It originated as a quick, portable fast-food option sold from street stalls for busy laborers in the 19th century.
